text: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on shigionoth.
LORD, I have heard the report of you, and I stand in awe. LORD, revive your work in the midst of the years; in the midst of the years make it known. In your wrath remember mercy.
God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.
His brightness is like the dawn; rays flash from his hand, and there his power lies hidden.
Before him goes pestilence, and plague follows at his heels.
He stood and measured the earth; he looked and made the nations tremble. The ancient mountains crumbled, the everlasting hills sank low—his ways are eternal.

versions.text: He stands, and the earth shakes; he looks, and the nations tremble. The ancient mountains are shattered, the everlasting hills sink low—his ways are eternal.
versions.explanation: The verb וַיְמֹדֶד is from מדד, "to measure"; rendering it "the earth shakes" loses the image of God surveying/apportioning the earth and creates an unnecessary duplication with the shaking imagery that follows. The tense also shifts oddly: the surrounding clauses in this verse describe completed action (perfect forms), so the past tense reads more consistently.

text: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress, the curtains of the land of Midian trembling.
Was the LORD angry with the rivers? Was your wrath against the streams, your fury against the sea, when you rode on your horses, on your chariots of salvation?

You uncovered your bow; you called for many arrows. Selah. You split the earth open with rivers. [Footnote: The Hebrew of this line is obscure; it may also be read "the oaths sworn to the tribes were a sure word."]

versions.text: You uncovered your bow; you called for many arrows. Selah. You split open the earth with rivers.
versions.explanation: This clause is one of the most difficult in the Hebrew Bible, and "you called for many arrows" reflects only one of several possible readings. A brief footnote alerting the hearer to the uncertainty adds value without disturbing the flow of the reading.

text: The mountains saw you and writhed; torrents of water swept by. The deep raised its voice and lifted its hands on high.
Sun and moon stood still in their places at the flash of your flying arrows, at the gleam of your lightning spear.
In fury you marched across the earth; in anger you trampled the nations.
You went out to deliver your people, to save your anointed one. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.

versions.text: You went out to deliver your people, to save your anointed one. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, stripping it bare from foundation to roof. Selah.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "from foundation to neck" (צַוָּאר), continuing the body imagery begun with "the head." "Roof" is an interpretive smoothing that breaks the deliberate wordplay between the crushed head and the exposed structure.

text: With his own spears you pierced the head of his warriors, who stormed out to scatter us, gloating as if to devour the poor in secret.
You trampled the sea with your horses, churning the mighty waters.

I heard, and my body trembled; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay crept into my bones, and my legs shook beneath me. Yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress, for the day when it comes upon the people who attack us.

Though the fig tree does not blossom and the vines bear no fruit, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the flock is cut off from the fold and there is no herd in the stalls—
yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
The LORD God is my strength; he makes my feet like the feet of a deer and sets me upon the heights. For the choirmaster, with my stringed instruments.
